name: Sint Maarten
summary: Sint Maarten's Book 4 (2014) abolished the legitieme portie, so there is no forced heirship; children and a spouse keep statutory lump-sum rights. Sint Maarten has its own trust (since 2014) and a private foundation. The Hague Trusts Convention is not in force for Sint Maarten.
family_claims: Book 4 gives a child a mandatory lump sum for care (art. 4:35) and for unpaid work in the household or business (art. 4:36); the spouse's position is strengthened. Wills for the benefit of an outsider can be attacked for abuse of circumstances (art. 4:43).
foreign_law_note: No source read states Sint Maarten's conflict rule for the estate of a foreign national.
trust_note: Only Curaçao appears in the Netherlands' extension list on HCCH, so the Convention is not in force for Sint Maarten. A trust has existed under Sint Maarten law since 1 April 2014 (secondary source). The stichting particulier fonds is listed in art. 2:1 of Book 2 (AB 2019 no. 43) and is exempt from the distribution ban for ordinary foundations.
open_questions: AB 2014 no. 6 takes effect on a date set by decree (art. XX); the commencement date was not found. The 2021 Dutch parliamentary question treats Sint Maarten as having no legitieme portie.
Conflict rule for succession of foreign nationals not sourced.
